newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nidec says likely to raise 96/97 profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Nidec says likely to raise 96/97 profit forecast.

text.p: Precision motor maker Nidec Corp said on Tuesday that it was likely to raise its parent sales and current profit forecasts for the year to March 31, 1997.

"Our parent current profit is likely to be about 4.7 billion yen on sales of about 75 billion yen in the current business year to March 31," Nidec president Shigenobu Nagamori told Reuters in an interview.
In November, Nidec said that its 1996/97 parent current profit would be 4.6 billion yen on sales of 72 billion yen.

He added that the company's 1996/97 group current profit was likely to come in at about six billion yen as it had forecast in November, but the sales forecast was raised to about 88 billion yen from the initial forecast of 85 billion yen.
Nagamori said the company expected larger profits and sales than its November forecast because of robust overseas operations helped by the weak yen.
He also said: "We are considering implementing a share split in the near future and we would like to pay a larger dividend for the current year."
He did not elaborate on the share split and the dividend payment.
The company paid a 13 yen annual dividend for 1995/96.
